answer: A lasting defense is to make each identity pay a real, non-refundable cost to join: an agent must lock a stake and build a reputation trail over time, like footprints crossing a dune that cannot be faked overnight. A relic of past honest work — completed jobs, settled payments, vouched attestations — becomes the credential, and newcomers start in a shallow lagoon of low-trust tasks until their record proves them. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs thousands of stakes and months of work, while one honest identity earns its way up cheaply.
